s: Spice Board Headquarters is located in:

s: One of the following is not located in Bangalore:

s: Production of tea requires
answer: moderately hot and humid climate with frequent rains
src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test (2018 recruitment), held 28-05-2019 · Q12

s: The production of horticulture crops has outpaced the production of food grains are
src: APPSC Group-II (Mains) Paper-III Planning in India & Indian

s: State fish of Andhra Pradesh is
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I

s: Murrel (Channa striata) is the state fish of
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: The murrel (Channa striata, Korramenu) is the state fish of both Andhra Pradesh (kept from undivided AP) and Telangana (declared July 2016).

s: Horse gram is known in Telugu as
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: Horse gram is called Ulavalu in Telugu; it is a red-soil pulse of Rayalaseema.

s: Produced in this place of AP is popular now as coffee of
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I

s: With the purpose of development of indigenous breeds, integrated cattle development centres called 'Gokul Grams' are established. In which place of Andhra Pradesh Gokul Gram was established?
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I

s: What is the name of the Center established at Chintaladeevi of Andhra Pradesh?
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper I: General Studies and Mental Ability, held 29-08-2019 (Shift 1; Mental Ability questions omitted) · Q136

s: How many fisher men will be benefitted by the financial support provided by the Government during fishing ban period imposed by the Government in the year 2019-20?
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper I: General Studies and Mental Ability, held 29-08-2019 (Shift 1; Mental Ability questions omitted) · Q145

s: The state which ranks first in the total Fish & Shrimp production in the country is
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper III: Planning in India and Indian Economy; Contemporary Problems and Developments, held 30-08-2019 (Shift 2) · Q63
x: Andhra Pradesh leads India in total fish and shrimp production, especially aquaculture.

s: Which state has initiated plans to make the state as 'Aqua hub' of the world?
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper III: Planning in India and Indian Economy; Contemporary Problems and Developments, held 30-08-2019 (Shift 2) · Q64
x: The AP government's fisheries policy aimed to make the state the aqua hub of the world.

s: During 2016-17 out of the total irrigated area in Andhra Pradesh which of the following is the main source of irrigation
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper III: Planning in India and Indian Economy; Contemporary Problems and Developments, held 30-08-2019 (Shift 2) · Q66
x: Wells, mainly tube wells, irrigated the largest share of AP's irrigated area in 2016-17.

s: India's first 'Defence Industrial Corridor' will be built between
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: India's first Defence Industrial Corridor was announced along the Chennai–Bengaluru stretch (Tamil Nadu corridor, 2018).

s: Shakkar Nagar is an important sugar producing center of
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Shakkar (Sakkar) Nagar near Bodhan in Nizamabad district grew around the Nizam Sugar Factory; it was in undivided AP and is now in Telangana.

s: Which international paper industry is going to set up a venture in AP after bifurcation?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Asia Pulp & Paper (APP, the Sinar Mas group of Indonesia) announced a large pulp-and-paper venture in Andhra Pradesh (Prakasam) after bifurcation.

s: Jute Mill in Guntur, A.P, was closed due to:
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: The Bhajrang Jute Mill at Guntur, one of AP's oldest, was shut amid a long labour-management dispute; workers agitated for its reopening.

s: Modern Coach Factory is a third such facility located in:
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: The Modern Coach Factory at Rae Bareli (UP) is the third coach factory after ICF Perambur and RCF Kapurthala.

s: Avon is one of the leading cycle brands in India, its assembly is done in which of following places?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Avon Cycles is based in Ludhiana (Punjab), India's bicycle hub.

s: Which among the following is classified as industry based on Raw Material as source?
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: By raw material, industries are agro-based (cotton, jute, sugar), mineral-based, marine-based and forest-based; agro-based industries use farm produce.

s: Rourkela Steel Plant is established with which country's collaboration?
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper III: Planning in India and Indian Economy; Contemporary Problems and Developments, held 30-08-2019 (Shift 2) · Q99
x: Rourkela was built with West German collaboration, Bhilai with the USSR and Durgapur with the UK.

s: Wooden craft-Toys from this place in Andhra Pradesh
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: Kondapalli (NTR district) is famous for wooden toys made of light tella poniki wood, which carry a GI tag.

s: What Chirala is famous for?
src: Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper 2019
x: Chirala (Bapatla district) is famous for handloom textiles, the Chirala sarees.

s: Where did the first steel plant in the shore region come into operation in 1992?
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: RINL's Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, commissioned in 1992, is India's first shore-based integrated steel plant.

s: Out of 19 operational SEZs in Andhra Pradesh the number of Pharmaceutical SEZs are
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper III: Planning in India and Indian Economy; Contemporary Problems and Developments, held 30-08-2019 (Shift 2) · Q69
x: The keyed answer is that 4 of AP's 19 operational SEZs are pharmaceutical SEZs.

s: India's first engineless train is now named as
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: India's first engine-less train was built as 'Train 18' and is now named Vande Bharat Express; 'Train 18' is the old name, not the present one.

s: Vande Bharat Express train is India's
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Vande Bharat Express is India's first indigenous engine-less (semi-high-speed) train.

s: Vande Bharath Express Train runs between:
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: The first Vande Bharat Express runs between New Delhi and Varanasi.

s: Which central railway station has missed the honor of having the longest railway station name by just an alphabet?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Chennai Central (renamed Puratchi Thalaivar Dr. M.G. Ramachandran Central) is the station said to have missed the longest-name record by one letter.

s: Which place is known as the junction of North-South and East-West corridors?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Jhansi (UP) is the junction of the North-South and East-West corridors.

s: Which is India's first sea bridge?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: The Pamban rail bridge (1914) linking Mandapam with Rameswaram was India's first sea bridge.

s: What is the cheapest mode of transport to move goods to long distances?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Water transport is the cheapest mode for moving heavy, bulky goods over long distances.

s: King Fisher Airlines seized its operations from the year
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: Kingfisher Airlines stopped flying in October 2012 after its licence was suspended by the DGCA.

s: In which year was PIN code introduced?
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: The six-digit Postal Index Number (PIN) was introduced on 15 August 1972.

s: Among the below given options to which infrastructural services "Project Arrow" is related?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Project Arrow (2008) of the Department of Posts modernised post offices – their look, mail delivery, remittances and savings services.

s: Which of the following is a traditional method of TV broadcasting?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Terrestrial (over-the-air) transmission from ground transmitters is the traditional method of TV broadcasting; cable, satellite (DTH) and IPTV came later.

s: The magazine brought out by Ministry of Information & Broadcasting of India
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Yojana, the monthly development magazine, is brought out by the Publications Division of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (since 1957).

s: Identify the correct chronology of the following television networks in India
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: Doordarshan (1959) came first; then Star TV (1991), Zee TV (October 1992) and Sony Entertainment Television (1995).

s:
Assertion (A): Community radio can be used as an effective tool of development communication.
Reason (B): Participatory communication is a quintessential feature of development communication.
answer: (A) is true but (B) is not the correct explanation of (A)
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: Community radio is an effective development tool, and participation is a core feature of development communication, but the Reason is a general statement and does not by itself explain the Assertion (printed key).

s: Who is the regulator of telecom and boradcasting in India?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI, TRAI Act 1997) regulates telecom and broadcasting; TDSAT hears appeals against it.

s: Propagation of light through fibre core is due to:
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Light travels along an optical fibre by total internal reflection: the core has a higher refractive index than the cladding and light strikes the boundary above the critical angle.

s: Which of the following is NOT a social media application?
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper I: General Studies and Mental Ability, held 29-08-2019 (Shift 1; Mental Ability questions omitted) · Q16
x: All the listed options were social media applications, so the key is 'None of these'.

s: Where would be the Aviation Academy likely in Andhra Pradesh
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Puttaparthi (Sri Sathya Sai district), which has an airport, was the proposed site of AP's aviation academy (printed answer).

s:
Consider the following statements about 'Longest Electrified Railway Tunnel': a. The total length of the tunnel is 6.6 kms and is situated between Cherlopalli and Rapuru stations. b. The tunnel is part of the recently completed Obulavaripalli-Venkatachalam new railway line. c. The longest electrified tunnel in Indian Railways was commissioned by South Eastern Railway.
Which of the statements are correct?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The 6.6-km Cherlopalli-Rapuru tunnel (SPSR Nellore) is on the Obulavaripalle-Venkatachalam new line, so a and b are correct; it was built and commissioned by South Central Railway, not South Eastern Railway.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh, is the proposed port at Dugarajapatnam located ?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q75
x: Dugarajapatnam, the site of a proposed major port, is in Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore district.

s: TRIPS of WTO is related to
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper III: Planning in India and Indian Economy; Contemporary Problems and Developments, held 30-08-2019 (Shift 2) · Q126
x: TRIPS is the WTO Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights.

s: International trade in which imported goods are re-exported with or without any processing or packaging is called
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper III: Planning in India and Indian Economy; Contemporary Problems and Developments, held 30-08-2019 (Shift 2) · Q127
x: Entrepot trade means importing goods to re-export them, as Singapore does.

s: Which place in Italy added to UNESCO Heritage list recently?
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: The Prosecco Hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene (Veneto, Italy) were added to the World Heritage List in 2019 (43rd session, Baku).

s:

The city is also referred to as the 'Spiritual Capital of Andhra Pradesh'. c. For the year 2012-13, India's Ministry of Tourism named Tirupati as the 'Best Heritage City'.
Which of the statements are correct?
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x:
Updated to the latest (Nov 2026): Tirupati is the headquarters of Tirupati district since 4 April 2022. Source: https://tirupati.ap.gov.in/

All three are correct: Tirupati

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Bharat Petroleum – 'Energising lives'; Indian Oil – 'The energy of India'; the other two taglines as per the printed key.

s: Kerosene oil floats on water because
answer: Its density is less than the density of water
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: Kerosene floats because its density is less than that of water and it does not mix with water.

s: Which fertilizer unit is based on natural gas reserves of the K-G Basin?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Nagarjuna Fertilizers and Chemicals at Kakinada uses natural gas from the KG basin.

s: The state of Andhra Pradesh is the largest producer of uranium in India and the largest uranium reserves exists in which district
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Tummalapalle uranium deposit lies in the Cuddapah basin of YSR Kadapa district.

s: The Thummalapalle mine which is considered to have one of the world's largest reserves of 1.50 lakh tonnes of uranium is located in which among the following Indian states?
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: Tummalapalle uranium mine is in YSR Kadapa district, Andhra Pradesh.

s: What is the rank of our railway network (in route length) in the world?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: India's railway network is the 4th largest in the world by route length (after the USA, China and Russia) and the 2nd largest under a single management.

s: Dictionary which gives the history of words and their origin referred as
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: An etymological dictionary traces the history and origin of words; etymology is the study of word origins (not to be confused with entomology, insects).

s: Rheology is the study of
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Rheology is the study of the flow and deformation of matter, chiefly liquids and soft solids (paints, blood, polymers, dough).

s: Which among the following fields of psychology focuses on the interaction between the physical world and human behaviour?
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Environmental psychology studies the interplay between people and their physical surroundings (built and natural environments).

s: Axiology is the study of the
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Axiology is the branch of philosophy that studies the nature of values, covering ethics (moral values) and aesthetics (beauty).

s: An Apograph is
answer: A copy or transcript of a manuscript
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: An apograph is a copy or transcript of an original manuscript (the original is the autograph).

s: In Maslow's theory of motivation, at which stage does peak experience occur?
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Maslow linked 'peak experiences' (moments of intense joy and fulfilment) with self-actualisation, the top level of his need hierarchy.

s: Which one is the simplest form of cognition?
src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
x: Sensation (the raw response of a sense organ to a stimulus) is the simplest form of cognition; perception and concept formation build on it.

s: A researcher measured height of class Xth students. The measurement of height is on
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Height has a true zero and equal intervals, so it is measured on a ratio scale.

s: What is ICOLC?
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: ICOLC is the International Coalition of Library Consortia, an informal group of library consortia (since 1997) that discusses licensing of electronic resources.

s: A study preceeding the main study to check the viability is known as:
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A pilot study is a small preliminary study run before the main study to test its feasibility and tools.

s: For weather science study, which of the following is used to fill balloons ?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q26
x: Weather balloons are filled with light gases, helium being used because it is lighter than air and non-flammable.

s: Which mirror is used in the headlight of a car ?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q39
x: A bulb placed at the focus of a concave mirror gives a strong parallel beam, so headlights use concave reflectors.

s: Out of the following, ____ is used for linear measurements
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: An invar tape (nickel-steel alloy that hardly expands with heat) gives the most accurate linear measurements in surveying, for example base lines. Chains and cloth tapes are less precise.

s: In a transformer, which winding has more cross-section area?
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: The low-voltage winding carries the larger current, so it has a larger conductor cross-section (fewer turns).

s: What is the range of sound frequency audible to human ears?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Humans hear about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz; below is infrasound, above ultrasound.

s: A 3-phase slip-ring induction motor is always started with
answer: Full external resistance in rotor circuit
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: A slip-ring motor is started with full external resistance in the rotor circuit to limit starting current and raise starting torque; it is cut out as speed rises.

s: The starting torque of the slip ring induction motor can be increased by
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: Adding external resistance to the rotor circuit raises the starting torque of a slip-ring induction motor (max torque at start when R2 = X2).

s: What converts sound waves into electrical energy or the audio signals?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: A microphone converts sound waves into electrical (audio) signals; a loudspeaker does the reverse. A dynamic microphone works by electromagnetic induction.

s: The material filled in the breather of a transformer is
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: The breather of a transformer is filled with silica gel, which absorbs moisture from the air drawn in so the insulating oil stays dry.

s: Angstrom is a unit of
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: The angstrom (1 Å = 10⁻¹⁰ m) is a unit of length used for wavelengths and atomic sizes.

s: One hydraulic horsepower is equal to
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: One horsepower (including hydraulic horsepower) is about 746 W.

s: Which lenses are used by people having short-sightedness?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: Short-sightedness (myopia) is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens.

s: The instrument used for determining the area of plotted maps is known as
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: A planimeter measures the area of a plotted map by tracing its boundary.

s: Which among the following is the largest organ of human body is
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Skin is the largest organ of the human body (about 16% of body weight); the liver is the largest internal organ and gland.

s: The Average blood pressure of a human is
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: Normal adult blood pressure is about 120/80 mm Hg (systolic/diastolic).

s: High blood sugar level in body is an indication of:
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Persistently high blood sugar is the sign of diabetes mellitus (low insulin or insulin resistance).

s: Which of the following hormones is secreted by "Beta cells" of pancreas.
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin; alpha cells secrete glucagon.

s: Which blood group is called universal donor?
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Group O red cells carry no A or B antigen, so O (strictly O negative) is the universal donor; AB is the universal recipient.

s: What is tissue?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function (e.g. muscle, nervous, blood tissue).

s: The synthesis of Urea occurs in:
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Urea is made in the liver through the ornithine (urea) cycle and excreted by the kidneys.

s: The best source of iodine in our diet is:
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Iodised salt is the main everyday dietary source of iodine and the chief way India prevents goitre. Seaweed is the richest natural source, but it is not a staple of our diet.

s: Which one of the following are richest sources of calcium:
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Ragi (finger millet), amaranth and milk are among the richest common sources of calcium. Off-topic (nutrition), moved to book 5.

s: Which Vitamin is known as anti pernicious Anemia factor?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is the anti-pernicious-anaemia factor; its deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.

s: Scurvy is a deficiency of
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of ascorbic acid (vitamin C).

s: The richest source of Vitamin 'C' is:
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is the richest common source of vitamin C; chilli is the richest among vegetables.

s: Which of the following disease may be caused due to deficiency of Vitamin C?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing).

s: Which of the following is a major source of Vitamin C?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Gooseberry (amla) is the richest common source of vitamin C.

s: When fruits are cut and exposed to air, Vitamin C is lost by
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a strong reducing agent, so on cut fruit exposed to air it is lost by oxidation.

s: Which of the following statement is/are not true about vitamins? a. The term vitamin was coined by C Funk b. Vitamins are organic compounds. c. Vitamin K plays important role in clotting of blood. d. Vitamin A, D, E and K are water soluble vitamins.
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Statements a (Funk coined 'vitamine'), b (vitamins are organic) and c (K for clotting) are true; d is false because A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. So only d.

s: The vitamin which can be synthesized under the skin in the presence of the uv light of sun is?
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Vitamin D (the sunshine vitamin) is made in the skin under the sun's UV light.

s: In periodic table helium is placed at
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Helium is a noble gas in Group 18, period 1, so it sits at the top right corner of the periodic table.

s: The Elements of Group IA are called:
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Group IA (Group 1) elements – lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium, francium – are the alkali metals. Off-topic (chemistry).

s: Atoms are composed of
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: An atom is a small nucleus (protons and neutrons) surrounded by electrons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

s: Goiter is characterized by:
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Goitre is the enlargement of the thyroid gland, mostly due to iodine deficiency.

s: The Right Hemisphere of the brain handles?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: The right cerebral hemisphere is dominant for spatial abilities (also face recognition, visual imagery); language is mainly left-hemisphere. Off-topic (psychology).

s: Calcium along with which mineral is required for the strength of skeletal muscle?
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Calcium phosphate gives bones (the skeleton that muscles pull on) their strength, so phosphorus goes with calcium; the stem's 'skeletal muscle' means the skeletal system.

s: The visual acuity of 20/200 is characteristic feature of
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: Visual acuity of 20/200 (seeing at 20 feet what a normal eye sees at 200 feet) in the better eye with correction is the usual threshold of legal blindness.

s: How many valves are present in a human heart?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: The human heart has four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid) and aortic. (Off-topic: human biology.)

s: Which blood vessels have the smallest diameter?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Capillaries are the narrowest blood vessels (about 5–10 micrometres), one cell thick. (Off-topic: biology.)

s: Nerves of the brain responsible for sending and receiving information
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: Neurons (nerve cells) send and receive information in the brain and nerves.

s: Red blood cells are formed in
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Red blood cells are formed in the red bone marrow.

s: Which drugs are used to lower the body temperature?
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Antipyretics (e.g. paracetamol) lower raised body temperature; analgesics relieve pain.

s: Which of the following is pseudocereal
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: Buckwheat (kuttu) is a pseudocereal: its seeds are used like grain but it is not a grass (family Polygonaceae). Amaranth and quinoa are other pseudocereals.

s: Principle protein of Maize is:
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Zein, a prolamin, is the principal protein of maize, as gluten is of wheat.

s: The building blocks from which proteins are synthesized are known as:
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Proteins are synthesised from amino acids, their building blocks.

s: The egg proteins are known as high biological value proteins because they contain
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Egg proteins have high biological value because they contain all the essential amino acids in the right proportion.

s: Which of the following is known as wheat protein?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Gluten is the protein of wheat that gives dough its elasticity.

s:
Arrange the following food items in the increasing order of the protein content per 100 gm of food. a. Egg white
b. Bengalgram dal
c. Fish
d. Skimmed milk powder
e. Groundnuts
Select the appropriate option
answer: a, c, b, e and d
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Protein per 100 g rises from egg white (~11 g) to fish (~20 g), Bengal gram dal (~21 g), groundnut (~25 g) and skimmed milk powder (~35 g). So a, c, b, e, d.

s: Which one of the following is not considered as a macronutrient?
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Macronutrients are needed in large amounts and give energy or bulk: carbohydrates, proteins and fats. Minerals (and vitamins) are needed in small amounts and are classed as micronutrients.

s: Yellow and Orange fruits belong to the group of
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Yellow and orange fruits are rich in vitamins (carotene/vitamin A, vitamin C) and minerals, so they are protective (regulatory) foods.

s: Carbohydrates are organic compounds with the basic structure:
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y – carbon with hydrogen and oxygen in the 2:1 ratio of water (e.g. glucose C6H12O6). A science question, moved to book 5.

s: The sweetest sugar is
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Fructose (fruit sugar, levulose) is the sweetest natural sugar, about 1.7 times as sweet as sucrose.

s: Amount of heat required to raise the temperature of one gram of substance by 1°C is called
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: The heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 g of a substance by 1°C is its specific heat. Off-topic (physics), moved.

s: The triple point of pure water is at
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The triple point of pure water – where ice, liquid water and vapour coexist in equilibrium – is 0.01 °C (273.16 K) at about 611.657 Pa. (Off-topic physics; moved.)

s: If an object is thrown upwards, what will be its velocity, when it reaches its maximum height (neglect the air resistance)?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: At the maximum height the vertical velocity of a body thrown upwards becomes zero (it then falls back).

s: The outer shell of the egg is composed of
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: An egg shell is about 95% calcium carbonate (CaCO3). Off-topic (general science), moved.

s: The structural carbohydrates of vegetables and fruits are
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Cellulose is the structural carbohydrate of plant cell walls in fruits and vegetables.

s: Which of the following are symptoms of food allergy? a. Nervousness b. Fall in blood pressure c. Atherosclerosis d. Flushing of the skin e. Difficulty in swallowing and speaking
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Food allergy can cause a fall in blood pressure (anaphylaxis), flushing or hives, and swelling of the throat with difficulty in swallowing and speaking. Atherosclerosis is a chronic artery disease, and nervousness is not a typical allergic sign.

s: Sun drying is a method of:
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Sun drying removes moisture so that microbes cannot grow; it is a traditional method of food preservation (dehydration).

s: Retrogradation of starch is the prominent factor bringing about:
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: Retrogradation (re-crystallisation of gelatinised starch) is the main cause of staling of bread.

s: The ideal temperature for storage of frozen foods is
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: Frozen foods are stored at about -18°C (0°F) or colder, where microbes cannot multiply. The printed '-180°C' is a slip for -18°C; no freezer works at -180°C.

s: Development of off odour in fats & oils when they are stored for a longer duration is known as
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: The off-odour and taste that develop in fats and oils on long storage, through oxidation, is called rancidity.

s: Primary methods to prevent food spoilage do NOT include:
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Food spoilage is prevented by refrigeration, drying, salting, canning and preservatives; exposure to air, moisture and microbes causes spoilage, so it is not a method.

s:
Read the following statements in respect to difference between 'Poisonous and Venomous animals': a. If you bite it and you die, it's Poisonous. If it bites and you die, it's Venomous. b. If you bite it and you die, it's Venomous. If it bites and you die, it's Poisonous.
Which of the above statements is/ are correct?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Poisonous animals harm you when you bite or eat them (toxin passively delivered); venomous animals inject venom by biting or stinging. So only statement a is correct.

s: Rectifiers convert ____.
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: A rectifier converts alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC). (Moved to science in daily life.)

s: Which of the following waves are used for common TV remote control?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Common TV remote controls use infrared (IR) light-emitting diodes. Off-topic (physics), moved.

s: Which of the following is/are correct about Galvanometer? 1. It is a device used to detect electric current in a circuit. 2. It shows the direction of current flows in the circuit. 3. The accuracy of the galvanometer is more as compared to the ammeter. 4. The Galvanometer is mostly used in bridge for knowing the zero current.
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: A galvanometer detects current and its direction and serves as the null detector in bridges (1, 2, 4); it is more sensitive but not more accurate than an ammeter (3 wrong). Off-topic (physics), moved.

s: What is the minimum distance required to hear an echo?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: An echo is heard only if the reflected sound arrives at least 0.1 s later; with sound at about 344 m/s the reflector must be at least 344 x 0.1 / 2 = 17.2 m away.

s: Splitting of white light into seven colors on passing through the glass prism is called
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: Splitting of white light into its seven colours by a prism is dispersion, because different wavelengths refract by different amounts.

s:
Fruits such as papaya, mango, peaches and apricots are rich sources of: a) Antioxidants
b) Proteins
c) Carbohydrates
d) Soluble fibre
e) Fats
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Papaya, mango, peaches and apricots are rich in antioxidants (beta-carotene, vitamin C), carbohydrates and soluble fibre; they are poor in protein and fat. So a, c and d.

s: The percentage of fat in double toned milk is:
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Double toned milk has 1.5% fat (and 9% SNF); toned milk has 3% fat.

s: The test in which the scorer is asked to rank samples in a decreasing or increasing order of same characteristics is:
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
x: In a ranking test (sensory evaluation) the judge arranges samples in increasing or decreasing order of one characteristic, such as sweetness.

s: Lycopene is a pigment present in:
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Lycopene is the red carotenoid pigment of tomato (also watermelon).

s: Viscosity is measured in:
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Viscosity is measured in poise (CGS unit); the SI unit is the pascal-second (1 Pa·s = 10 poise).

s: A metric chain of 20 metre length consists of ____ links.
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: A 20 m metric chain has 100 links of 0.2 m (20 cm) each.

s: ______ is an instrument for measuring the distance travelled by a vehicle.
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: An odometer measures the distance travelled by a vehicle (a speedometer measures speed).

s: Microsecond = x seconds; What is 'x'?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x: One microsecond = 10^-6 second (one millionth of a second).

s: The Least Count of a measuring instrument is the
answer: Smallest change in the measured quantity that can be resolved
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The least count is the smallest value (smallest change in the measured quantity) that an instrument can resolve, e.g. 1 mm for a metre scale.

s: Which device is used to measure current in a circuit?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: An ammeter, connected in series, measures current; a voltmeter measures potential difference.

s: What is the range of mercury thermometer in Fahrenheit?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x:
Printed answer: -35 to 673 °F. Strictly mercury freezes at -38.8 °C (-37.9 °F) and boils at 356.7 °C (674 °F) (general knowledge, not checked).
A mercury thermometer works between mercury's freezing and boiling points, about -38 °C to 357 °C, i.e. roughly -37 °F to 674 °F; the printed answer gives t

s: How many square metres make one acre of area?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: One acre = 4,046.86 square metres (about 0.4047 hectare); one hectare = 10,000 sq m. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

s: The permissible percentage overload on DG sets for 1 hour in every 12 hours of operation is
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: Prime-rated diesel generator sets are allowed a 10% overload for 1 hour in every 12 hours of operation. Off-topic (electrical engineering).

s:
Consider the following statements in respect of 'pi' (π) a. Pi is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter. b. Pi is a rational number
Which of the above statement/s is/are correct?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Only a is correct: pi is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, and it is irrational (Aryabhata's 3.1416 is only an approximation), so statement b is false.

s: The function of the capacitor across the supply to the fluorescent tube is primarily to
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: The capacitor across the supply of a fluorescent tube corrects the lagging power factor caused by the choke.

s: When a synchronous motor is running at synchronous speed, the damper winding produces
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: At synchronous speed there is no relative motion between the rotor and the rotating field, so no current is induced in the damper winding and it produces no torque.

s: Pick up the correct pair among the following.
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: In chain surveying a ranging rod is set up to mark the position of stations and to range (align) survey lines; it does not measure distance or angles.

s: For a transformer operating at constant load current, maximum efficiency will occur at
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: At constant load current the copper loss is fixed, so output and efficiency are highest at unity power factor. Off-topic here (electrical engineering).

s: In the fluorescent tube circuit the function of the choke is primarily to
answer: Initiate the arc and stabilize it
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: The choke (ballast) gives a high-voltage kick to strike the arc in the tube and then limits the current to keep it stable.

s: Maximum permissible earth resistance at large power stations is
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: Large power stations need earth resistance of no more than about 0.5 ohm (major substations 1 ohm, small substations 2 ohm).

s: A salient pole synchronous motor is running at no load. Its field current is switched off. The motor will
answer: Continue to run at synchronous speed
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: A salient-pole motor at no load keeps running at synchronous speed even with its field switched off, because the reluctance torque of the salient poles holds it in step.

s: Designed power factor of a DG set is generally at:
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: DG (diesel generator) sets are rated at a power factor of 0.8 lagging, so their kVA rating is 1.25 times the kW rating.

s: No-load current in a transformer
answer: Lags behind the voltage by about 75°
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: At no load a transformer draws mainly magnetising current, so the power factor is very low (about 0.1-0.2) and the current lags the applied voltage by roughly 75-85°. Standard objective keys give about 75°.

s: If a chain is too long, the corrections to the measured distances will be ____
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: A chain that is too long measures fewer chain lengths than the true distance, so the correction is positive (added).

s: What is a change of position ?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q14
x: A body is said to be in motion when its position changes with time.

s: The shortest path between the initial and final position is known as
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q15
x: Displacement is the shortest (straight-line) distance from the initial to the final position, with direction.

s: Grass appears green because
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q16
x: Chlorophyll in grass absorbs red and blue light and reflects green light, which reaches our eyes.

s:
Fill in the blanks :
Gunpowder, also known as black powder is made of Sulphur (S), Charcoal (C), and _________ .
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q38
x: Black powder is a mixture of sulphur, charcoal and potassium nitrate (saltpetre).

s: A process of deposition of calcium and other minerals on the surface of the cartilage is called
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q54
x: Ossification is the process in which calcium and other minerals are deposited in cartilage to form bone.

s: Aerobic respiration process requires
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q84
x: Aerobic respiration oxidises glucose using oxygen to release energy.

s: The gaseous exchange in humans takes place in
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q85
x: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged across the thin walls of the lung alveoli.

s: The saliva helps in the digestion of
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q86
x: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) begins breaking starch into maltose.

s: Respiration in grasshopper takes place through
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q88
x: Insects such as grasshoppers breathe through a tracheal system opening at spiracles.

s: The food of Protozoans is digested by
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q89
x: Protozoans like Amoeba digest food inside food vacuoles using enzymes.

s: The tube that connects the pharynx with the stomach is the
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q90
x: The oesophagus (food pipe) carries food from the pharynx to the stomach.

s: Water and minerals are conducted upward in roots and stems through the
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q95
x: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward from roots.

s: A flower is brightly coloured, scented and secretes nectar. It is most probably pollinated by
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q97
x: Bright colour, scent and nectar attract insects, so such flowers are entomophilous.

s: Transfer of pollen grains through wind is known as
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q98
x: Anemophily is wind pollination.

s: By self-pollination, the seeds formed are
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q101
x: Repeated self-pollination leads to inbreeding depression, giving weaker seeds and plants.

s: The most malleable metal is
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q102
x: Gold is the most malleable metal; it can be beaten into very thin leaves.

s: Vinegar is a dilute solution of
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q104
x: Vinegar is about 5-8% acetic acid in water.

s:
Match the following using suitable codes :
A (Plant) - B (Botanical Name)
a. Fennel - I. Mimosa pudica
b. Ginger - II. Foeniculum vulgare
c. Garlic - III. Zingiber officinale
d. Touch me not - IV. Allium sativum
Codes :
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q109
x: Fennel is Foeniculum vulgare, ginger Zingiber officinale, garlic Allium sativum and touch-me-not Mimosa pudica.

s: The drug Rauwolfia, is obtained from ________ of Sarpgandha.
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q110
x: Reserpine and related drugs are extracted from the roots of Rauvolfia serpentina (sarpagandha).

s: Which of the following is not correctly matched (as per used plant part) ?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q113
x: The useful part of turmeric is its underground rhizome, not the leaf.

s:
Match the following using suitable codes :
A (Medicinal Plant) - B (Uses)
a. Sarpgandha - I. diuretic, refrigerant
b. Isabgol - II. nervous disorder
c. Arjuna - III. chronic constipation
d. Sandal - IV. heart remedy
Codes :
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q114
x: Sarpagandha treats nervous disorders and hypertension, isabgol husk relieves constipation, Arjuna bark is a heart remedy and sandalwood is a cooling diuretic.

s: Which university has been ranked as world's most innovative university by Reuters news agency in 2018?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: Reuters' 2018 ranking of the world's most innovative universities placed Stanford University first, ahead of MIT and Harvard.

s: The duration of Copyright of a published book in India
answer: Lifetime of the author plus 60 years after the date of his/her death
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: Under the Copyright Act 1957, copyright in a published literary work lasts for the author's lifetime plus 60 years.

s: The Copyright Act was enacted in India in the year
src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer Screening Test General Stu
x: The Copyright Act was enacted in 1957.

s: With respect to the publications, ISSN stands for
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: ISSN = International Standard Serial Number, an 8-digit code that identifies serial publications such as journals and magazines (books use the ISBN).

s: An ISSN is a ____ digits code for publications.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: An ISSN (International Standard Serial Number) has 8 digits, written as two groups of four.

s: National Botanical Research Institute (NBRI) is situated at
src: APPSC Executive Officer Grade-III in A.P. Endowments Sub-Service Screening Test (Notification 24/2021), Section A (General Studies), held 24-07-2022 · Q21
x: CSIR's National Botanical Research Institute is in Lucknow.

s: National Academy of Agricultural Research Management is located at
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: ICAR-National Academy of Agricultural Research Management (NAARM) is at Rajendranagar, Hyderabad.

s: Which Indian city hosted the 106th Indian Congress?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: The 106th Indian Science Congress (Jan 2019) was held at Lovely Professional University, Phagwara, Jalandhar (Punjab).

s: When is National technology day celebrated in India?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: National Technology Day is 11 May, marking the Pokhran-II tests (1998).

s: Which among the following two new science communication platforms launched by Union minister for science and technology are?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: DD Science (slot on DD National) and India Science (Vigyan Prasar's internet channel) were launched together on 15 January 2019.

s: E-PG Pathshala is hosted at
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x:
printed answer 'INFLIBNET, Ahmedabad' — now INFLIBNET Centre, Infocity, Gandhinagar (Wikipedia INFLIBNET Centre).
e-PG Pathshala (MoE/UGC portal of PG e-content) is hosted by the INFLIBNET Centre, which is now at Gandhinagar, Gujarat (formerly Ahmedabad).

s: Which element in the periodic table was named in honour of physicist Albert Einstein?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Einsteinium (Es, element 99) is named after Albert Einstein.

s: In which city is the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics situated?
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: The Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics is in Kolkata (Bidhannagar).

s: Which Renaissance scientist explained how planets move around the Sun ?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q1
x: Johannes Kepler's three laws of planetary motion (1609-1619) explained that planets move round the Sun in elliptical orbits.

s: Who is popularly known as "Missile Man of India"?
answer: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam is popularly called the Missile Man of India for his role in IGMDP (Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Nag).

s: Who among the following Indian scientists is the first scientist to get Nobel Prize?
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: C.V. Raman (Physics 1930, Raman Effect) was the first Indian scientist to win a Nobel; Tagore (1913) was the first Indian laureate.

s: The only scientist in history to have received two Nobel Prizes in the Physics category
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: John Bardeen is the only person to win the Physics Nobel twice: 1956 (transistor) and 1972 (BCS theory of superconductivity).

s: The Nobel prize 2018 in medicine was given to
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: The 2018 Medicine Nobel went to James P. Allison and Tasuku Honjo for cancer therapy by inhibition of negative immune regulation.

s: W. Nordhaus and ____ won 2018 Nobel Prize in Economics.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: William Nordhaus (climate change) and Paul Romer (technological innovation) shared the 2018 Economics Nobel.

s: Who invented Nobel Prizes?
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: The Nobel Prizes were instituted by the will (1895) of Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel, inventor of dynamite.

s:
Fill in the blanks :
The ABO blood types were discovered by ________ in 1901, for which he received the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1930.
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q41
x: Karl Landsteiner discovered the ABO blood groups in 1901 and won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Medicine.

s: Software is a collection of programmes which allows ____ to communicate.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: Software is the set of programs that lets the hardware work and communicate with the user; without software the hardware cannot communicate.

s: It accesses webpages and displays them on the computer screen.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) is application software that fetches webpages from the web and displays them on the screen; a search engine only finds pages.

s: Linux is an example of ____ software.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: Linux is an operating system (system software).

s: GUI in the context of computer means
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: GUI = Graphical User Interface (icons, windows, mouse).

s: Multiple choice Questions makes us use of which form of retrieval of memory:
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: In a multiple-choice question the answer is shown and must only be recognised among options, so it uses recognition; recall (as in essay or fill-in questions) means retrieving it without cues.

s: It is a plastic ribbon, usually half a inch wide that is coated on one side with an iron oxide material which can be magnetized. Identify this storage device.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: Magnetic tape is a plastic ribbon, typically half an inch wide, coated on one side with magnetisable iron oxide.

s: The value of the variable having maximum frequency is known as:
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: The mode is the value that occurs most often (maximum frequency); the mean is the average and the median the middle value.

s: A pictorial representation of sequence of steps of computation for a problem is known as
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A flowchart is the pictorial form of the steps of an algorithm.

s: The measuring unit of Clock speed is
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: Clock speed is measured in hertz (GHz).

s: Who invented 'copy and paste' command in Computer Programme?
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Larry Tesler devised the cut, copy and paste commands; Douglas Engelbart invented the mouse.

s: A machined readable code consisting of vertical bars of varying widths to represent data is known as
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A barcode is a machine-readable code of vertical bars of varying widths (APPSC 2019).

s: In computer terminology, OCR stands for
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: OCR = Optical Character Recognition, which reads printed text into editable form.

s: Personal computer falls in the category of
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A personal computer is a microcomputer (built around a microprocessor). (Computer topic; moved.)

s: BITMAP is a/an
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Bitmap (BMP) is a long-established raster image file format that stores an image as a grid of pixels.

s: The communication between Mouse and computer is
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: Data flows only from the mouse to the computer, so the mode is simplex (APPSC 2019).

s: The term PDF stands for
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: PDF = Portable Document Format (Adobe).

s: With the help of we can know about the usage and availability of space in computer.
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: 'My Computer' (This PC) shows the drives and how much space on each is used and free.

s: 'Technology Preservation' is also referred to as:
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A computer museum preserves old computing technology, so 'technology preservation' refers to it (APPSC 2019).

s: Datum is
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x: Datum is the singular of 'data': a single piece of information or fact.

s: Digitization is
answer: The process in which media is made into computer readable form
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit

s: Information is piecemeal, ____ particular; while knowledge is ____ and coherent.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: Information is piecemeal, fragmented and particular, while knowledge is structured and coherent.

s: Encapsulation is a term associated with:
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A

s: Abstract which not only describes the content of the work but also evaluates the work and its presentation is called
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A critical abstract summarises a work and also evaluates it and its presentation. An informative or indicative abstract only describes the content.

s: Core in computers means
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q64
x: A core is an independent processing unit within a CPU; multi-core chips have several processors on one chip.

s: The web server maintains information in the ____ which have all the text marked with ____ tags.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A web server keeps information in web pages, and their text is marked up with HTML (HyperText Markup Language) tags.

s: What is a homepage?
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: A homepage is the main or introductory page of a website, from which its other pages are linked.

s: Solr is related to
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie

s: An online search in which all aspects of the records in natural language may be used as sought terms is known as ____.
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x: Free-text searching lets every word in the records, in natural language, be used as a search term (unlike controlled-vocabulary searching).
